chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zur'arah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from 'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'When does the dowry become obligatory?' He said, 'When he consummates the marriage with her.'
ai.seo_question: When does the dowry become obligatory in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) specifies that the full obligation of the dowry (mahr) is contingent upon consummation (dakhala biha), distinguishing this from mere contract or cohabitation. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining financial rights in cases of divorce or death prior to consummation, reflecting the principle that the complete exchange of value requires physical union. The narration, transmitted through a reliable chain in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the legal precision applied to marital financial obligations.
